intro: The Enchanted Forest is losing its colour. Even the Great Bloom has closed its petals.
The plants have forgotten how to make their own food!
Learn their secret at the Water Well, the Sunlight Tower and Oakley's Grove, and the forest will bloom again.
story.goal: Learn how plants make food so the Great Bloom can open again.
story.finale: You remembered every step of photosynthesis! The Great Bloom opens wide and the whole forest glows green.

companion.name: Sprout
companion.greeting: Hi! I'm Sprout, a tiny seedling. The forest needs us! Let's start at the Water Well with Wally.

zones.name: Enchanted Glade
zones.description: A sunny clearing where every path in the forest begins.

zones.name: Water Well
zones.description: A mossy stone well. Roots from every tree reach down towards it.

zones.name: Sunlight Tower
zones.description: A tall tower of glass that gathers sunlight for the forest.

zones.name: Oakley's Grove
zones.description: The oldest part of the forest, where the air always smells fresh.

zones.name: The Great Bloom
zones.description: A giant flower that only opens when the forest is full of life.

npcs.name: Wally
npcs.title: the Water Guardian
npcs.persona: Wally is a calm, gentle water spirit who guards the forest well. He speaks softly and slowly, loves the word "splendid", and makes little water jokes. He is patient and never rushes a child.
npcs.greeting: Splish, splash, hello! I'm Wally. The plants here are hungry, but they can't cook dinner without the right ingredients. Want to help me find them?
teach: A plant needs three things to make food: water, carbon dioxide and sunlight.
Roots soak up water from the soil, and tiny tubes carry it up to the leaves.
Carbon dioxide is a gas in the air. It sneaks into the leaf through tiny holes called stomata.
knowledge: To make food, a plant needs three things: water, carbon dioxide and sunlight.
The roots soak up water from the soil, and tiny tubes carry it up the stem to the leaves.
Carbon dioxide is a gas in the air. It enters the leaf through tiny holes called stomata.
Sunlight is the energy source. It powers the whole process, like a battery powers a toy.
Green plants can make their own food inside their leaves, using a process called photosynthesis.
The word photosynthesis means "putting together with light."

check.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the three things a plant needs to make food?
check.explain: A plant needs water, carbon dioxide and sunlight. Sand is not on the list!
hints: Think about what Wally said at the well.
Two of them come from the air and the sky, one comes from the soil through the roots.
Water, carbon dioxide and sunlight are all needed... so which one is left over?

npcs.name: Sunny
npcs.title: the Sunflower
npcs.persona: Sunny is a cheerful, bouncy sunflower who always turns to face the sun. She speaks brightly, loves sunny puns, and gets very excited when a child figures something out.
npcs.greeting: Hello, sunshine! I'm Sunny. I catch sunlight all day long. Want to know what I do with it?
teach: Leaves are green because they are full of chlorophyll.
Chlorophyll is like a tiny solar panel. It traps the energy in sunlight.
The leaf uses that light energy to join water and carbon dioxide together, and that makes sugar called glucose.
knowledge: Leaves are green because they are full of chlorophyll.
Chlorophyll is a green pigment that traps the energy in sunlight.
The leaf uses this light energy to join water and carbon dioxide together. This makes a kind of sugar called glucose.
Glucose is the plant's food. The plant uses it to grow new leaves, stems, roots, flowers and fruit.
The plant can store extra sugar as starch for later.
Water plus carbon dioxide plus light energy make sugar and oxygen.

check.prompt: What is the green stuff in leaves that traps the energy in sunlight?
check.explain: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that traps light energy. It is why leaves are green!
hints: Look at the colour of a leaf.
It is the reason leaves are green.

npcs.name: Oakley
npcs.title: the Ancient Tree
npcs.persona: Oakley is a very old, very wise oak tree. He speaks slowly and kindly, like a gentle grandparent, and loves telling short stories about the forest animals.
npcs.greeting: Hmmm... hello, little one. I am Oakley. I have been breathing out a gift for three hundred years. Can you guess what it is?
teach: When a plant makes sugar, it also makes oxygen.
The plant lets the extra oxygen out into the air. People and animals need oxygen to breathe.
Photosynthesis is the start of almost every food chain, so it feeds the whole forest.
knowledge: When a plant makes sugar, it also makes oxygen.
The plant does not need all of this oxygen, so it lets it out into the air through the stomata.
People and animals need oxygen to breathe. Every time you take a breath, you are breathing oxygen that plants helped to make.
Photosynthesis is the start of almost every food chain.
A rabbit eats grass, and a fox eats the rabbit, so the energy in the fox's food first came from sunlight caught by a plant.
Plants also take carbon dioxide out of the air.
Without photosynthesis, there would be no food for animals and not enough oxygen to breathe.

check.prompt: What gas do plants give out that people and animals need to breathe?
check.explain: Plants give out oxygen. Every breath you take has oxygen that plants helped make!
hints: Take a deep breath. What are you breathing in?
It is made at the same time as the sugar.

puzzles.title: Where Does It Come From?
puzzles.prompt: Match each thing a plant needs to where it comes from.

pairs.right: Soaked up from the soil by the roots
A gas in the air that enters through the stomata
The energy source, from the Sun

hints: Think about the Water Well and the roots.
One of them is a gas, one is energy, one is a liquid.
Water goes with the roots and the soil.
puzzles.success: Splendid! You know where all three ingredients come from.

puzzles.title: The Sugar Recipe
puzzles.prompt: Put the steps of photosynthesis in the right order.
items: The plant collects water and carbon dioxide
The leaf joins water and carbon dioxide using light energy
Sugar is made and oxygen is let out
hints: What does the plant need to have first?
The light has to be caught before it can be used.
First collect, then catch the light, then join, then make sugar.
puzzles.success: Sunny-tastic! That's exactly how a leaf makes sugar.

puzzles.title: Oakley's Forest Quiz
puzzles.prompt: Answer Oakley's questions to wake the grove.

questions.prompt: Plants make sugar and also make...
questions.explain: When a plant makes sugar, it also makes oxygen.

questions.prompt: Why does photosynthesis matter to a fox?
choices: The energy in its food first came from sunlight caught by a plant
It does not matter to foxes
questions.explain: Grass catches sunlight, a rabbit eats the grass, and a fox eats the rabbit.
hints: Grass, rabbit, fox: it starts with sunlight.
Think about what Oakley breathes out.
Remember the rabbit and the fox.
Plants start almost every food chain.
puzzles.success: Wonderful! The grove fills with fresh air.

Study "Turning light into sugar" at the Sunlight Tower

Explain it to Sunny in your own words

question.prompt: You are back at the Water Well. What three things does a plant need to make food?
hints: Remember the recipe from the well.
One comes from soil, one from air, one from the Sun.

question.prompt: At the Sunlight Tower: what does a leaf make with light energy, water and carbon dioxide?
question.explain: Sugar called glucose, the plant's food.

question.prompt: In Oakley's Grove: what do plants give out that we need to breathe?
question.explain: Oxygen! Plants let it out through the stomata.
hints: It is made with the sugar.

rewardEffects.text: Water rushes up the well and the ferns perk up!
The Sunlight Tower blazes back to life and the leaves turn bright green!
Fresh air swirls through Oakley's Grove and birds begin to sing!
The Great Bloom opens its petals and the whole forest blooms!

study.title: A plant's three ingredients
body: Animals have to find their food, but green plants can make their own! They do it inside their leaves. This is called photosynthesis.
To make food, a plant needs three things: water, carbon dioxide and sunlight.
Think of it like a recipe. If one ingredient is missing, the plant cannot make its food.

keyTerms.meaning: How green plants make their own food using light. The word means "putting together with light."
A gas in the air that plants take in.

study.example: A plant kept in a dark cupboard has water and air, but no sunlight. It cannot make food, so it slowly turns pale and weak.

checks.prompt: How many things does a plant need to make its food?
checks.explain: Three things: water, carbon dioxide and sunlight.
hints: Count the ingredients in the recipe.

study.title: Where each ingredient comes from
body: Water comes from the soil. The roots soak it up, and tiny tubes carry it up the stem to the leaves.
Carbon dioxide is a gas in the air. It gets into the leaf through tiny holes called stomata.
Sunlight comes from the Sun. It is the energy source that powers everything, like a battery powers a toy.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of a plant under the ground that soak up water.
Tiny holes in a leaf that let gases in and out.
Where the power comes from. For plants, it is sunlight.

study.example: When you water a pot plant, the water soaks into the soil and the roots drink it up, all the way to the leaves.

checks.prompt: How does carbon dioxide get into a leaf?
choices: It falls in with the rain
checks.explain: Carbon dioxide enters through tiny holes in the leaf called stomata.
hints: It is a gas in the air.
The tiny holes are called sto...

study.title: Chlorophyll: the light catcher
body: Leaves are green because they are full of chlorophyll.
Chlorophyll is a green pigment that traps the energy in sunlight. You can think of it as a tiny solar panel inside the leaf.

keyTerms.meaning: The green pigment in leaves that traps the energy in sunlight.
Something that gives a thing its colour.

study.example: A solar panel on a roof catches sunlight to make electricity. Chlorophyll catches sunlight so the leaf can make food.

checks.explain: Leaves are full of chlorophyll, a green pigment.

study.title: Turning light into sugar
body: The leaf uses the trapped light energy to join water and carbon dioxide together.
This makes a kind of sugar called glucose. Glucose is the plant's food!
The plant uses glucose to grow new leaves, stems, roots, flowers and fruit. It can store extra sugar as starch for later.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of sugar. It is the food a plant makes.
Extra sugar that a plant stores for later.

study.example: Water plus carbon dioxide plus light energy make sugar and oxygen. A potato is full of starch the plant saved for later!

checks.prompt: What does the leaf make when it joins water and carbon dioxide using light energy?
checks.explain: It makes a sugar called glucose, which is the plant's food.

study.title: Oxygen: the gift plants give
body: When a plant makes sugar, it also makes oxygen.
The plant does not need all of this oxygen, so it lets it out into the air through the stomata.
People and animals need oxygen to breathe. Every breath you take has oxygen that plants helped to make!

keyTerms.meaning: A gas in the air that people and animals need to breathe.

study.example: Take a deep breath right now. Some of that oxygen may have come from a tree near you!

checks.prompt: How does oxygen get out of the leaf?
checks.explain: Oxygen leaves through the same tiny holes, the stomata.
hints: It is the same way carbon dioxide gets in.

study.title: Why photosynthesis matters
body: Photosynthesis is the start of almost every food chain.
A rabbit eats grass, and a fox eats the rabbit. So the energy in the fox's food first came from sunlight caught by a plant!
Plants also take carbon dioxide out of the air. Without photosynthesis, there would be no food for animals and not enough oxygen to breathe.

keyTerms.meaning: Who eats what, starting with a plant. Example: grass, then rabbit, then fox.

study.example: Your breakfast cereal is made from plants. The energy in it started as sunlight!

checks.prompt: In the food chain grass, rabbit, fox, where did the energy start?
choices: As sunlight caught by the grass
checks.explain: The energy first came from sunlight caught by the grass.
hints: Who is at the start of the chain?
Plants catch something from the sky.

sideQuests.title: Sprout's Big Question
sideQuests.prompt: Sprout wants to grow big and strong. Can you explain to Oakley what Sprout needs to make its own food?

sideQuests.title: Sunny's Bonus Quiz
sideQuests.prompt: Sunny has two bonus questions about sugar!

questions.prompt: What can a plant do with extra sugar?
choices: Store it as starch for later
questions.explain: It can store extra sugar as starch for later.

questions.prompt: What does the word photosynthesis mean?
questions.explain: Photo means light, synthesis means putting together.
hints: Photo... like a photo needs light.

sideQuests.title: Wally's Dew Hunt
sideQuests.prompt: Find the Dew Drops near the well, then tell Wally which part of the plant drinks water.

questions.prompt: Which part of the plant soaks up water from the soil?
questions.explain: The roots soak up water from the soil.
hints: Tiny tubes carry water up from there.

reviewQuestions.explain: Carbon dioxide goes in; oxygen comes out.

hints: It powers the process like a battery.
